strings.temp_expired_feedback: {count} local execution approvals expired; nothing started.
strings.approval_expires_in: Approval expires in {time}; no execution after expiry
strings.approval_skipped: {count} requests were no longer valid and were not authorized.
strings.approval_expired_feedback: {count} call approvals expired; no authorization granted.
strings.approval_detail_invalid: This request was cancelled or expired. Details closed without granting authorization.
strings.approval_detail_scope: The buttons decide this entire call, including all its hosts and commands. Authorization lasts from this call's launch to completion.
strings.approval_unlock_text: These calls read host passwords from your Bitwarden vault, which is locked. Enter the master password to unlock it and allow them in one step; the session is kept according to the re-authentication policy.
strings.approval_single_subtitle: Codex asks to run {commands} command(s) on {hosts}. Nothing starts until you allow it.
strings.approval_batch_subtitle: Codex has {count} calls waiting. The buttons decide the calls listed below, and only those.
strings.approval_new_arrivals: {count} more calls arrived while this list was open.
strings.approval_key_hint: Esc rejects the calls shown. Opening details decides nothing.
strings.approval_detail_key_hint: Esc returns to the list without deciding.
strings.temp_approval_subtitle: Codex asks to run a local program with {fields} temporary secrets passed as environment variables. Nothing starts until you allow it.
strings.temp_more_waiting: {count} more runs are waiting after this one.
strings.temp_key_hint: Esc rejects this run. Opening details decides nothing.
strings.temp_blocked_running: Another operation is running. Wait for it to finish or stop it before allowing this run.
strings.temp_detail_scope: Authorize only this local run. Going back makes no decision. Secrets are shown as field names only.
strings.temp_input_revoked: Fields or approval settings changed; {count} waiting operations cancelled.
strings.validation_sudo: Password-record usernames must be nonempty and unique, with no CR, LF or NUL.
strings.su_hint: Use the target account's saved password when su asks for it. Passwordless execution still works when this is off. Remote PAM permissions are unchanged.
strings.privilege_password_renamed: Renaming discards the old user's password. A new password is optional.
strings.sudo_password_missing: No password saved; passwordless sudo/su needs none.
strings.sudo_invalid_password: A user password cannot contain CR, LF or NUL.
strings.sudo_hint: Reuse the SSH login password when sudo asks for it. A separately saved account password takes priority. Passwordless or cached authentication still works when this is off; remote permissions are unchanged.
strings.sudo_password_cleared: Separate password removed on save; an eligible login password can still be used.
strings.hosts_refreshed: The hosts were changed elsewhere; your unsaved changes to this host are kept.
strings.host_changed: This host changed in another window. Review your draft, then reselect the host to load the saved version.
strings.tray_unavailable: Tray is unavailable; the window remains open.
strings.temp_memory_notice: Memory only. Cleared on exit or system restart.
strings.temp_delete_all_confirm: Delete all {count} fields, including saved values and unsaved drafts? This cannot be undone.
strings.temp_delete_all_running: Waiting operations will be cancelled. Already running programs will not be stopped.
strings.temp_no_fields: No temporary secrets. Add a field above to get started.
strings.temp_fields_changed: The field list changed. Review it before choosing Delete all again.
strings.sudo_system_password_hint: Password for SSH account {user}. Normally needed only for key or Agent login; removing it does not disable login-password reuse.
strings.temp_replace_hint: Saved. Enter a replacement to update.
strings.temp_invalid_field: Use 1–64 unique names, up to 256 bytes, without control characters.
strings.temp_invalid_value: Enter a non-empty value up to 32 KiB, without NUL. Whitespace is preserved.
strings.temp_field_approval_hint: On: approve each call using this field. Off: allow direct execution. New fields default to on.
strings.temp_global_approval_hint: Turns call approval on or off for every field at once, and for fields added later until codex-hosts exits. Each field can still be changed on its own; a dash means they differ. Changing it cancels waiting runs.
strings.temp_approval_off_body: Programs Codex runs with these secrets will start without asking you. This also applies to fields added later and stays in effect after codex-hosts restarts, until you turn it back on. Waiting runs are cancelled.
strings.temp_approval_off_title: Turn off call approval for all fields?
strings.temp_global_approval_hint: Turns call approval on or off for every field at once and for fields added later; the choice is kept after codex-hosts restarts. Each field can still be changed on its own; a dash means they differ. Changing it cancels waiting runs.
strings.temp_activity_idle: No runs yet. Runs that use these secrets appear here.
strings.ssh_call_approval_hint: Off by default. When enabled, approval covers only the current Codex call, from launch to completion, including its listed commands. Session retention does not extend approval.
strings.editor_subtitle: Passwords and file passphrases are stored in Windows Credential Manager. FIDO PINs are never saved; hardware private keys stay on the device.
strings.no_password_hint: An empty password will be used for authentication.
strings.password_saved: Saved. Leave blank to keep the existing password.
strings.password_required: Enter a password, or select No password.
strings.terminal_login_title: Log in from a terminal (when the wizard cannot finish the login)
strings.terminal_login_text: Run these lines in your own PowerShell; the login is written to the same data directory, so you can unlock here afterwards.
strings.unlock_prompt_title: Codex needs the Bitwarden master password
strings.unlock_prompt_text: A tool call needs a host password from your Bitwarden vault. Enter the master password to unlock it; the session is kept according to the re-authentication policy.
strings.credential_services_hint: See the services that hold host credentials, switch them on or off, and open each service's management page.
strings.bw_disabled_hint: Bitwarden is switched off: its hosts are hidden and refuse to connect until it is enabled again.
strings.bw_not_configured: Bitwarden is not set up yet.
strings.bw_policy_hint: How long codex-hosts keeps the vault unlocked. Every call: each use asks for the master password; the next unlock makes the previous key useless. Idle: locked once unused for that many minutes. Until codex-hosts closes: locked when the main window exits. Permanent: until you press Lock or Bitwarden rejects the key. Whenever codex-hosts ends a key it also runs bw lock, so the bw CLI is locked as well. The key is kept in Windows Credential Manager, like saved passwords.
strings.bw_policy_locked_now: Every call is now required: the kept key was removed and the vault locked.
strings.bw_setup_done: Bitwarden is set up; the Login items of the chosen folder appear as hosts under “Bitwarden”.
strings.back_to_services_hint: Back to the list of credential services
strings.bw_done_text: The Bitwarden account {account} is connected. The Login items in the folder "{place}" appear as hosts in the Bitwarden group of the host list and are read from the vault again before each use.
strings.bw_done_next_add: To save a host in Bitwarden, choose "New host" → "Bitwarden host"; it is stored as a Login item in that folder.
strings.bw_done_next_edit: Changes made to those items in the web vault or on another device apply the next time the host is used.
strings.bw_done_store_error: The unlocked session could not be kept in Windows Credential Manager ({error}); you will need to unlock again after closing codex-hosts.
strings.bw_signed_out_hint: This account is signed out. Choose "Log in again…" to sign in and verify in the setup wizard.
strings.bw_confirm_logout: After logging out, Bitwarden hosts cannot be used until you log in again, which may require a new-device code. Log out?
strings.bw_confirm_remove: Removing the setup disconnects this Bitwarden account and removes its hosts from the list. The items in your vault are not changed. Remove the setup?
strings.vault_chip_hint: Bitwarden status; click to open the Bitwarden page.
strings.host_actions_hint: More host actions: import, test all, batch management
strings.bw_err_locked: The vault is locked. Unlock it with the master password on the Account tab.
strings.bw_err_signed_out: Not logged in to Bitwarden. Log in again under Credential services.
strings.bw_err_verification: Bitwarden needs a two-step or new-device code.
strings.bw_err_network: bw could not reach the server (network, proxy, or certificate problem).
strings.bw_err_invalid_credentials: The email or master password is incorrect.
strings.bw_err_item_missing: The vault item is missing, in the trash, or has no password.
strings.bw_err_item_mismatch: The vault item is not a Login item or its account differs from the host account.
strings.bw_err_sync: The vault could not be synced; retry or check the connection.
strings.bw_err_cli_unverified: This bw version is not on the verified list; writes are refused.
strings.wizard_cli_hint: Point at the official native Bitwarden CLI (bw.exe). codex-hosts runs it as a child process and never embeds an HTTP stack of its own.
strings.wizard_login_hint: The master password stays in this window's memory and reaches bw only through the child process environment; it is never written to disk.
strings.wizard_new_device_text: Bitwarden has e-mailed a new-device verification code to {email}. Enter the code from that message. This login waits for it, so no further code is sent meanwhile.
strings.wizard_two_step_text: Enter the two-step login code: the one your authenticator app shows, the one Bitwarden has just e-mailed, or touch your YubiKey.
strings.wizard_method_text: This account has several two-step login methods. Choose the one to use; with Email, Bitwarden sends the code when you continue.
strings.wizard_retry_hint: Logging in again makes Bitwarden send a new code when the account needs one; enter the code from that newest message.
strings.wizard_unexpected_prompt: bw asked for input this window cannot answer (for example single sign-on). Log in from a terminal below.
strings.bw_err_invalid_code: Bitwarden rejected the code. Make sure it comes from the newest message and has not expired.
strings.wizard_folder_text: Choose the folder in your Bitwarden vault whose Login items become hosts. Each item needs a name (the host alias), an ssh:// or telnet:// URI, a username and a password; the custom fields codex-hosts:description and codex-hosts:tags carry the remark and the tags.
strings.wizard_policy_text: When should codex-hosts ask for the master password again?
strings.private_key_hint: Select a regular OpenSSH private-key file or a *_sk file created for a hardware key.
strings.fido_direct_hint: After selecting a *_sk file, Windows uses the connected hardware key directly. SSH Agent, Pageant, and vendor software do not need to be running.
strings.fido_found: Found the SSH file for hardware key {fingerprint}. The matching hardware key is checked when connecting.
strings.fido_not_found: No usable hardware-key SSH file was found. Recover an existing credential from the key or create a new one.
strings.fido_setup_hint: Create or recover an SSH-specific credential.
strings.fido_pin_hint: Leave this empty when creating or recovering a recoverable credential; Windows requests the PIN itself. It may be needed here only for compatible creation and is never saved or logged.
strings.fido_recover_existing: A recoverable SSH credential already exists on the hardware key. Choose Recover an existing credential from the key instead of creating another one.
strings.fido_create_recommended: Create a credential recoverable from the key
strings.fido_create_recommended_hint: The credential is stored on the security key. Select the YubiKey and enter its PIN in Windows Security; no key file needs to be copied to another computer.
strings.fido_enrollment_cancelled: Windows Security was cancelled or not completed within 45 seconds. No credential was created.
strings.fido_recover: Recover an existing credential from the key
strings.fido_recover_hint: After changing computers or losing the local files, recreate what SSH needs by completing two Windows Security prompts. Select the same ssh: credential on the same hardware key both times.
strings.fido_recovery_cancelled: Windows Security prompt {step} of 2 was cancelled or timed out. Start recovery again and complete both prompts.
strings.fido_create_compatible: Create a compatible credential (copy file to another computer)
strings.fido_create_compatible_hint: For security keys that cannot store the credential on the device. On another computer you need both the hardware key and the key file created here; if that file is lost, the hardware key alone cannot recover it.
strings.fido_wait_touch: Waiting for Windows Security; follow its prompt and touch the hardware key if requested…
strings.fido_setup_succeeded: SSH key file saved for {fingerprint}. Authorize the public key below on the target server before connecting.
strings.copy_public_key: Copy public key for server authorization
strings.passphrase_saved: Saved. Leave blank to keep the existing passphrase.
strings.passphrase_optional: Only needed when the selected file is encrypted. Do not enter the hardware-key PIN here.
strings.agent_key_hint: Optional. Leave blank to try identities exposed by the running SSH Agent or Pageant in order. codex-hosts does not read a key file in this mode.
strings.chain_hint: Only verified SSH hosts can be selected. Nested jump hosts are followed automatically.
strings.host_key_unverified: Not trusted yet. Testing will request confirmation.
strings.test_all_empty: There are no saved hosts to test.
strings.status_test_timeout: Connection test failed: the allowed time expired.
strings.telnet_warning: Telnet sends credentials and session data without encryption. Use it only on a trusted network.
strings.fingerprint_new_message: No host key is stored for {alias}. Verify this SHA-256 fingerprint through a trusted channel before continuing.
strings.fingerprint_changed_message: The host key for {alias} differs from the trusted value. Continue only if this change is expected and independently verified.
strings.validation_address: An IP address or host name is required.
strings.validation_private_key: Select a regular OpenSSH private-key file or the *_sk file for a hardware key.
strings.validation_chain: The selected jump-host chain is invalid or contains a loop.
strings.validation_telnet_chain: Telnet hosts cannot use or provide a jump host.
strings.codex_draft: Codex prepared this draft. Complete the required fields, then save or cancel.
strings.delete_message: The host entry will be removed. Credentials will also be deleted from Windows Credential Manager.
strings.import_hint: Download the CSV template and complete the host fields. Extra columns are ignored. Passwords and private-key passphrases may be imported into Windows Credential Manager; the source CSV remains sensitive until deleted.
strings.template_save_failed: Could not save the import template: {error}
strings.import_succeeded: Imported {count} host(s). Add any missing credentials and test each connection before use.
strings.import_succeeded_with_credentials: Imported {count} host(s) and stored their credentials in Windows Credential Manager.
strings.import_cleanup_message: The imported CSV contains passwords or private-key passphrases in plaintext. Delete {path} now to reduce the risk of credential exposure?
strings.import_file_deleted: Imported {count} host(s) and deleted the sensitive CSV: {path}.
strings.import_file_delete_failed: The sensitive CSV remains at {path} because it could not be deleted: {error}
strings.import_file_kept_warning: Warning: the CSV at {path} still contains plaintext credentials. Protect or delete it as soon as possible.
strings.batch_select_hint: Select the hosts to manage, then choose Delete, Export, or Cancel.
strings.batch_delete_message: The {count} selected host entries and their Windows Credential Manager credentials will be deleted.
strings.batch_export_hint: Credentials and private-key contents are never exported. Exporting to a directory automatically chooses a new numbered file; choosing a specific file allows that exact path to be replaced.
strings.chain_in_use: Used as a jump host by another saved entry and cannot be deleted.
strings.unsaved_changes: Connection details changed. Test verification will be cleared when saved.
strings.secret_not_exported: Passwords, passphrases, and PINs are never shown in plaintext, logged, or returned to Codex.
strings.editor_empty_hint: Select a host on the left, or create a new one.
strings.validation_auth_persistence: Idle minutes must be between 1 and 1440.
strings.validation_advanced: An advanced setting is out of range.
strings.persistence_telnet_note: Telnet always re-authenticates on every operation.
strings.persistence_warning_ssh: While the session is kept, later Codex commands on this host run without re-authenticating or touching the security key. That removes the one-confirmation-per-action protection. Enable it only for hosts you are willing to let Codex operate continuously.
strings.persistence_first_message: Host "{alias}" will use "{to}". This decides how often Codex must authenticate (and touch a hardware key) on this host.
strings.persistence_change_message: Host "{alias}": "{from}" → "{to}". This changes how often Codex must authenticate (and touch a hardware key) on this host.
strings.persistence_retained_hint: Keeps its authenticated session between Codex calls.
strings.fingerprint_reported_by_codex: Reported by Codex — compare it with the server before trusting.
strings.max_channels_hint: Upper bound on command session channels open on this host at once (sshd MaxSessions): exec_many concurrency and, for kept sessions, parallel Codex calls. Tunnels through a jump host are not counted. Default 8.
strings.timeout_default_hint: Used when Codex does not pass a timeout; an explicit value in the call still wins. Defaults: 120 s to connect, 600 s per command.
strings.keepalive_hint: How often a kept session pings the server; lower it behind aggressive NAT. Only applies when the session is kept.
strings.remote_env_hint: A hint for Codex only (shell family for batches and background jobs); codex-hosts never acts on it.
strings.codex_hidden_hint: Codex will not see or use this host; it stays available here.
strings.telnet_prompts_hint: Override the login and password prompt text for devices whose banners differ from the defaults.
strings.store_owner_unavailable: The owner of the host list file could not be checked ({error}). Codex access may be refused.
strings.store_owner_warning: The host list file is owned by another account ({owner}). Codex access will be refused until it is yours again: {command}
strings.su_accounts_hint: Optional passwords for other accounts, usually the target of su. Passwordless execution needs none. These records do not choose an execution user.
strings.login_password_user_changed: The login user changed. Enter the new user's password; the previous user's password will not be reused.
strings.bw_intro: Bitwarden hosts live in one folder of your vault: every Login item there (name, ssh:// or telnet:// URI, username, password) is a host and stays in step with the vault. Set the account up to use it.
strings.bw_sync_window_hint: How old the local vault copy may be when a Bitwarden host is used. “Before every use” picks up changes made in the web vault or on another device at once (calls that follow each other within a few seconds share one sync); a longer window saves a bw sync per call.
strings.vault_items_text: The Login items of the folder. An item is served as a host when it has a name, an ssh:// or telnet:// URI and a username; the others say what is missing.
strings.vault_fix_text: Enter the endpoint and account for this item. The vault is updated and the host appears after the next refresh.
strings.vault_problem_name_taken: name already used by another host
strings.vault_section_unloaded: The Bitwarden folder has not been read yet.
strings.vault_section_locked: The vault is locked. Unlock it to see its hosts.
strings.vault_section_empty: The folder holds no hosts yet. Add one with "＋ New host".
strings.vault_refresh_hint: Read the folder from Bitwarden again
strings.vault_refreshed_with_problems: Read {count} hosts from Bitwarden; {problems} items are not hosts (see Credential services → Bitwarden → Folder items).
strings.vault_unlock_hint: Enter the master password to unlock the vault and read the hosts in its folder
strings.vault_login_hint: The account is signed out; open the Bitwarden page to log in again
strings.vault_section_signed_out: The account is signed out. Log in to see its hosts.
strings.unsaved_switch_message: The changes to this host have not been saved. Discard them and continue?
strings.vault_host_hint: This host is its Bitwarden item. Name, endpoint, account, password, description and tags are written to the item on save and follow changes made in the vault; the remaining settings in this form stay in codex-hosts.
strings.vault_host_fields_hint: Each Login item of the folder is a host: its name is the alias, its first ssh:// or telnet:// URI the endpoint (user@host:port), its username and password the login; the custom fields codex-hosts:description and codex-hosts:tags carry the remark and the tags.
strings.vault_password_hint: The password lives in the Bitwarden item; type a new one here to replace it.
strings.vault_delete_message: The host's Bitwarden item is moved to the vault trash (restorable there) and its local settings are removed.
strings.vault_conflict: The item changed in Bitwarden since it was opened; refresh and edit again.
strings.unlock_prompt_window_text: Enter the master password to read or write Bitwarden hosts.
strings.wizard_login_text: Sign in to the Bitwarden account that holds (or will hold) the hosts folder.
strings.wizard_folder_none: The vault has no folders yet.
strings.wizard_folder_hint: An existing folder keeps its items: those with an ssh:// or telnet:// URI become hosts at once. A new folder starts empty.
strings.new_vault_host_hint: Add a host whose item lives in the Bitwarden folder
strings.services_intro: Host credentials can live in any of the services below. Each service forms its own group in the host list; hosts are added to a group from its ＋ button or from “New host”.
strings.service_local_text: Passwords and key passphrases of local hosts, stored under the signed-in Windows account. Connection details stay in this app.
strings.service_bitwarden_text: The Login items of one vault folder are the hosts: name, ssh:// or telnet:// URI, username and password; description and tags in codex-hosts:… custom fields. Read through the official bw CLI and synchronised before use.
strings.revert_changes_hint: Drop the unsaved changes and show the saved host again
strings.wizard_terminal_title: Log in from a terminal (when this window cannot finish the login)
strings.wizard_terminal_text: Run these lines in your own PowerShell, type the code at the prompt, then press the button below.
strings.wizard_still_signed_out: The account is still signed out. Finish the terminal login first.
strings.service_onepassword_text: The Login items of one vault are the hosts: title, ssh:// or telnet:// URL, username and password; description and tags in a codex-hosts section. Read and written through the official op CLI with the 1Password app, which asks you to allow codex-hosts.
strings.op_install_hint: The 1Password CLI was not found. Install it, then press Search again:
strings.op_problems: {count} items are not used as hosts: {names}
strings.op_section_empty: No hosts yet. Add Login items with an ssh:// or telnet:// URL to the vault, then Refresh.
strings.op_host_hint: This host is its 1Password item. Name, endpoint, account, password, description and tags are written to the item on save and read again before every use; the remaining settings in this form stay in codex-hosts.
strings.op_password_hint: The password lives in the 1Password item; type a new one here to replace it.
strings.op_new_host_hint: Add a host whose item lives in the 1Password vault
strings.op_delete_message: The host's 1Password item is moved to the archive (restorable in 1Password) and its local settings are removed.
strings.op_conflict: The item changed in 1Password since it was opened; refresh and edit again.
strings.op_chip_hint: 1Password status; click to open the 1Password page.
strings.op_done_text: The 1Password account {account} is connected. The Login items in the vault "{place}" appear as hosts in the 1Password group of the host list and are read from 1Password again before each use.
strings.op_done_next_add: To save a host in 1Password, choose "New host" → "1Password host"; it is stored as a Login item in that vault.
strings.op_done_next_edit: Changes made to those items in the 1Password app apply the next time the host is used; items added there appear after Refresh.
strings.op_cli_hint: codex-hosts talks to the 1Password app through its official command-line tool, op.exe. Its location was searched for below; check it, or choose the file.
strings.op_integration_hint: In the 1Password app, turn on Settings › Developer › "Integrate with 1Password CLI", and keep the app running and unlocked.
strings.op_prompt_title: 1Password will ask you to allow codex-hosts
strings.op_prompt_text: A 1Password window, "1Password requests authorization" with "Allow codex-hosts to get CLI access", appears, possibly behind this window. Press Authorize there and confirm with Windows Hello or your account password. It asks again after 10 idle minutes, and at least every 12 hours.
strings.op_waiting_prompt: Waiting for 1Password… approve the prompt in the 1Password window.
strings.op_vault_text: Choose the vault whose Login items are the hosts. A vault of its own is recommended: codex-hosts reads and writes the Login items in it.
strings.op_confirm_remove: Remove the 1Password setup from codex-hosts? Its hosts leave the list; the items stay in 1Password.
strings.op_section_unloaded: Not read yet. Press Refresh to read the vault; 1Password asks you to allow codex-hosts.
strings.op_section_not_authorized: 1Password did not allow codex-hosts. Unlock the app, press Refresh and approve its prompt.
strings.op_section_app_closed: The 1Password app is not running. Open it, then press Refresh.
strings.op_err_not_cli: The chosen file is not the 1Password CLI (op.exe 2.x).
strings.op_err_integration: Turn on Settings › Developer › "Integrate with 1Password CLI" in the 1Password app, then try again.
strings.op_err_app: The 1Password app did not answer. Open it, then try again.
strings.op_err_not_authorized: 1Password did not allow the request: unlock the app and approve its prompt, then try again.
strings.op_err_item_missing: The 1Password item behind this host no longer exists.
strings.op_err_vault_name: Enter a vault name of up to 100 characters that does not start with "-".
strings.op_err_disabled: 1Password is switched off in codex-hosts; enable it in the credential services.
strings.transfer_copy_hint: The originals stay where they are. Host names are unique across every store, so each copy is named after its original with -copy at the end.
strings.transfer_move_hint: Each original is removed once its copy is saved: a local host leaves this list and Windows Credential Manager, a password-manager item goes to its trash or archive (restorable there).
strings.transfer_secrets_hint: The login password goes straight from the source to the target and is never shown. Key passphrases, sudo and su passwords, host-key trust and the Advanced settings come along.
strings.transfer_skipped: {count} of them are already in {target} and are skipped.
strings.transfer_no_target: Set up Bitwarden or 1Password under Credential services to move or copy hosts there.
strings.transfer_nothing: The selected hosts are already in {target}.
strings.transfer_unsaved: Save or revert the open host first.
strings.transfer_source_left: {alias} is now in {target}, but its original item could not be removed ({error}). Remove it in {source}.
strings.transfer_conflict: If {target} already has the host or its name
strings.transfer_on_skip_hint: The host is left out and nothing in {target} changes.
strings.transfer_on_overwrite_hint: The existing host in {target} takes this host's server, login, password and settings; a moved host also gives it its name. If this host has no password, the existing one is kept.
strings.transfer_on_keep_hint: The host is added next to the existing one, with a number after its name (for example web-2).
strings.transfer_all_skipped: Nothing was transferred: {target} already has these hosts.
strings.batch_deleting_items: Moving {count} password-manager items to their trash or archive…
strings.batch_delete_vault_note: Bitwarden items go to the vault trash and 1Password items to the archive, where they can be restored.
strings.batch_delete_item_failed: {count} items could not be deleted, so their hosts stay. {alias}: {error}
